title: Target dual-rAF frame-step jitter, deliberately not reproduced
statement:
Target dual-rAF frame-step jitter is intentionally not reproduced.

The deterministic one-frame publication delay remains.

The exception covers only raw frame-step scheduling irregularity.
It does not cover final position, travel, decay, pointer orbit,
touch behaviour, wrap continuity or the filtered camera-dolly envelope.

whatTheTargetDoes.architecture: the Target computes its motion in framer-motion's frame loop and paints it in r3f's -- two independent requestAnimationFrame callbacks reading and writing the same motion values. We compute and paint in one.
whatTheTargetDoes.measuredMechanism: M1 described this as dropped frames: 'a frame on which framer did not tick repaints the same value, and the next frame carries double'. The M2 measurement does not support that and corrects it. The Target's frame interval is as steady as ours -- 8.3 ms median -- and it has essentially no near-zero steps and no double steps. What it has is a smooth spread of the per-frame step around its own local trend, roughly 0.89x to 1.13x. That is a continuous PHASE difference between the loop that solves the spring and the loop that samples it, not a loop that misses beats.

whatIsKept: The one-frame publication delay is DETERMINISTIC and is kept. It is not part of this exception: the Target's renderer consumes the motion values from a frame callback that runs before the model's own, so what reaches the screen is always the previous frame's value, and we do the same thing on purpose. Replayed against the Target's own recorded trajectory, one frame beats nought and two on every single sequence.

coversNothingElse.note: every landmark below is product-gated and a FAIL on any of them is a FAIL, exception or no exception

waysOfReproducingItThatAreForbidden: creating two competing rAF loops to race each other
generating a race tuned to one machine's refresh rate
whyForbidden: each of them would put a scheduling irregularity into the product on purpose. A page that skips or repeats frames to look like another page is worse than the page it is imitating, and a pattern tuned to one refresh rate is a defect on every other.
theOnlyRemedyThatWouldBeAllowed: if -- and only if -- the SCHEDULER-INVARIANT camera-dolly envelope still failed, a single deterministic sampling adapter could be designed. It would have to be proved identical at 60, 90 and 120 Hz and it could not change a single motion contract constant. This round did not reach that condition; see filteredDollyEnvelope below.
